## Purpose and entry points
MediaCMS is a self-hosted video/media portal: upload, catalog, publish, share/embed, stream, and manage video, audio, images, and PDFs. The primary application is Django, entered through `manage.py`, configured/routed by `cms/settings.py` and `cms/urls.py`, and served in production through `cms/wsgi.py`. Its browser UI is a compiled React asset set built from `frontend/src/static/js/pages/index.ts`.

## Core media domain and API
The `files` Django app owns the central persistence model: media, encodings, categories, subtitles, playlists, pages, comments, ratings, and related video metadata. Key model boundaries are `files/models/media.py`, `files/models/encoding.py`, and `files/models/category.py`. HTTP/API operations are grouped by resource in `files/views/media.py`, `files/views/encoding.py`, and `files/urls.py`; serializers in `files/serializers.py` form the API representation boundary.

## Upload-to-processing flow
Clients upload resumable/chunked source files through the dedicated uploader app (`uploader/urls.py`, `uploader/views.py`, `uploader/fineuploader.py`). Media records and source storage are then handled by the files domain and storage abstraction (`files/models/media.py`, `files/backends.py`). Processing is asynchronous: `files/tasks.py` dispatches background work through the Celery application in `cms/celery.py`, separating interactive request handling from costly transcoding, thumbnail/derivative, HLS, subtitle/transcription, and trim-related work.

## Playback, editing, and delivery
Published media views expose playback/embed experiences through `files/views/media.py` and server templates such as `templates/cms/media.html` and `templates/cms/embed.html`. The primary UI has media-page/viewer components at `frontend/src/static/js/pages/MediaPage.js` and `frontend/src/static/js/components/media-viewer/VideoViewer/index.js`. A separately built Video.js player is maintained in `frontend-tools/video-js/src/VideoJS.jsx`. Standalone React tools for video trimming and chapter editing call backend video APIs: `frontend-tools/video-editor/client/src/services/videoApi.ts` and `frontend-tools/chapters-editor/client/src/services/videoApi.ts`; their built artifacts are served under `static/video_editor` and `static/chapters_editor`.

## Identity, authorization, and external learning systems
Authorization is layered: Django-level permission/auth customization (`cms/auth_backends.py`, `cms/permissions.py`), media-specific checks (`files/permissions.py`), and persisted RBAC groups (`rbac/models.py`). Local user/account behavior resides in `users/models.py` and `users/views.py`. Federated SAML integration is isolated in `saml_auth/adapter.py` and `saml_auth/views.py`; configurable identity-provider mappings live in `identity_providers/models.py`. LTI 1.3 launch/deep-link flows are bounded in `lti/urls.py`, `lti/handlers.py`, and `lti/deep_linking.py`; a Moodle integration is distributed in `lms-plugins/mediacms-moodle`.

## Frontend composition
The main frontend is not a separate SPA deployment; Django templates load page-specific compiled assets from `static/js`. Source pages/components in `frontend/src/static/js/pages` consume backend APIs and shared contexts/stores, e.g. `frontend/src/static/js/utils/settings/api.js` and `frontend/src/static/js/utils/stores/MediaPageStore.js`. Server templates provide base markup and installation/runtime configuration (`templates/base.html`, `templates/config/index.html`), creating a server-rendered shell plus React-enhanced screens boundary.

## Runtime and deployment topology
The supported stack is Python/Django/DRF with PostgreSQL persistence, Redis-backed Celery messaging, FFmpeg/Bento4 media processing, Nginx proxy/static delivery, and Gunicorn web workers. Docker Compose manifests (`docker-compose.yaml`, `docker-compose.full.yaml`) define local/full environments. Container startup scripts in `deploy/docker/entrypoint.sh` and `deploy/docker/prestart.sh` coordinate initialization; Supervisor definitions explicitly run Gunicorn, Nginx, and separate short/long/beat Celery processes (`deploy/docker/supervisord/supervisord-gunicorn.conf`, `deploy/docker/supervisord/supervisord-celery_long.conf`).
